claims.claim: Along any nonnegative C1 demand curve on an open interval with constant complete minimum-route regime, equilibrium edge loads are C1; E is C1; S and P are C1 if z c_e(z) strictly convex.
claims.hypotheses: C1 nonnegative nondecreasing costs with c'_e(z)>0 for z>0; finite route sets (restricted allowed); demands may vanish; interior points only.

claims.claim: S and the Beckmann value are C1 along C1 demand curves with the same feasible set as the equilibrium; E=tV' on rays.
claims.hypotheses: convex C1 edge objectives with strictly increasing derivative (for S: z c_e(z) strictly convex; convexity alone does not give a unique optimum).

claims.claim: The one-sided endpoint version at t0=0 fails in general.
claims.hypotheses: oscillating C1 costs, not BPR; BPR endpoint case open.

claims.claim: Weak slope inequalities of CDS Thm 4.4(i) hold at nested breakpoints (expansions and contractions) for costs with zero slope only at zero load, including BPR with a_e>=0 and edge-specific exponents.
claims.hypotheses: proportional demand t r, t0>0, nested regimes. PoA statement needs z c_e(z) strictly convex (true for BPR).

claims.claim: For almost every free-flow vector a, every nondegenerate nested breakpoint has a strict slope jump.
claims.hypotheses: c_e=a_e+phi_e, phi_e C1 with phi'>0 on (0,inf); r>0; nondegenerate = all edges on routes of the smaller regime loaded at t0; degenerate case open. PoA statement needs z c_e(z) strictly convex.

claims.claim: Three-link strictly convex example with E,P in C4\C5 at an expansion.
Three-link BPR-type contraction with edge-specific exponents (4,2,6), E,P in C4\C5.
Five-link common-quartic expansion with E,P in C4\C5; x=(84/125)delta^3; E-E0=-(84672/78125)delta^5; bank-swapped contraction likewise.
claims.hypotheses: positive BPR coefficients, all simple paths, proportional demand.

claims.claim: m+2 links give x in C^{m-1}\C^m and E,P in C^{2m-2}\C^{2m-1} for every real p>1 and odd m>=3.
At most four edges: strict slope jumps at every nested breakpoint; five links minimal for expansions and contractions.
claims.hypotheses: a_e,b_e>0, common p>1, all simple paths, r_k>0, nested breakpoints.

claims.claim: Mixed BPR exponents: contractions need exactly 3 links; expansions need 4 or 5.
S and P are C^{2m-1}\C^{2m} at t=1/gamma; P^(6) jump about +89.68 in the five-link example.
claims.hypotheses: family of Thm 5.3; P statement needs E C^{2m} near 1/gamma, verified for the five-link example by exact interval arithmetic.
claims.status: proof (S); proof for P conditional on E being C^{2m} near 1/gamma, checked exactly for the quartic example; numerical jump value

claims.claim: Kinks return at size |eps|^{2-2/m} under free-flow or demand-ratio perturbation; transverse demand directions give C1\C2.
Hidden activation table, tolerance windows, near-match kinks, S(1)=19.762875963175, P(1)=1.0120, P^(5) jump -6.58.
Sioux Falls: no link activation for theta in [0.5,1.5]; two transverse activations near theta=0.259-0.260 with linear growth and 3.3-3.4% slope drops; loose tolerances misreport link usage.
claims.hypotheses: one test network, uniform demand scaling, link-level only.

claims.claim: Contact budget r-1, synthesis of any finite odd pattern with exactly 2+sum m_j edges, local threshold prescription, eight-link double contact.
Pinned contact of order m has codimension m-1 in a congestion-coefficient chart; a three-link C-infinity example.
claims.hypotheses: specified charts; smooth nonanalytic costs for the flat example.
